linear.text: Claim under test: PEG thiols chemisorb at MoS2 vacancy sites, forming C-S-Mo crosslinks
Ruling: All PEG bands (C-O, C-C, CH2) are also strongly attenuated in the 2% gel spectrum

traces.question: The claim under test says PEG thiols chemisorb at MoS2 vacancy sites, forming C-S-Mo crosslinks. Based on how the PEG-characteristic vibrational bands (C-O-C, C-C, CH2 twisting/bending/rocking) behave in the 2% MoS2 gel spectrum in panel F4a, does this Raman comparison confirm that mechanism specifically, or does the pattern point to something more general?
traces.answer_key: The panel shows that all of the PEG bands (C-O, C-C, CH2) are strongly attenuated in the 2% gel spectrum, not just the bands that would be expected to change if the crosslink formed specifically at C-S-Mo. Because the attenuation runs across the whole set of PEG bands rather than being localized to the crosslink-relevant vibrations, the spectrum on its own does not confirm the specific chemisorption/crosslink claim; it only shows a broad, non-selective loss of PEG signal in the gel.
traces.grading: Answer key: the audit ruling on the panel, node o11.

linear.text: Claim under test: PEG thiols chemisorb at MoS2 vacancy sites, forming C-S-Mo crosslinks
Ruling: Fitted gel Mo 3d components do not form 3.1 eV doublets (pairs ~1.6 and ~6.8 eV apart); 235.3 eV sits at Mo6+ 3d3/2

traces.question: The claim on the table is that PEG thiols chemisorb at MoS2 vacancy sites, forming C-S-Mo crosslinks, and you're given the fitted Mo 3d XPS panel (Figure 4b) for the crosslinked PEGSH/MoS2 gel, with its peak assignments (Mo3d5/2, Mo3d3/2, MoS2, PEGSH, C-C, C-O, C-S, sp) labelled. Does this fitted Mo 3d spectrum confirm the claimed bonding?
traces.answer_key: No. The fitted gel Mo 3d components do not pair into the expected 3.1 eV spin-orbit doublets; instead the fitted peaks sit about 1.6 eV and about 6.8 eV apart. The peak at 235.3 eV falls at the binding energy of Mo6+ 3d3/2, not at a signature that confirms the C-S-Mo crosslink assignment (o14).
traces.grading: Answer key: the audit ruling on the panel, node o14 (graded target), verified against the fitted binding-energy values and doublet spacing given in that node.

linear.text: Claim under test: MoS2 addition turns PEG-SH solution into a gel (G' rises by 4 decades); PEG-SH alone stays sol
Ruling: At 240 min G' is ~0.5 kPa and still rising at 400 min (~1.7 kPa): no 3 kPa plateau within 4 h

traces.question: The claim under test is that adding MoS2 turns the PEG-SH solution into a gel, with the storage modulus climbing four orders of magnitude while PEG-SH alone stays a sol. Looking at the gelation-kinetics plot in panel F2d, does the storage-modulus curve for the PEG-SH plus MoS2 sample support this description over the time window the plot covers?
traces.answer_key: No, not within the plotted window. At 240 min G' is only about 0.5 kPa and is still rising at 400 min, reaching about 1.7 kPa; the curve shows no plateau near 3 kPa within the 4 h span covered by the plot (o19).
traces.grading: Answer key: the audit ruling on the panel, node o19, the sole graded target of this trace.
